summary: P. De Lacy Johnstone (1848–1927) was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Edinburgh, at the University of Oxford as a Boden Sanskrit Scholar (~1867–1870), and at Balliol College, Oxford (1868–1876, B.A., M.A.).
P. H. Joshi is an Indologist. He held posts at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, serving as a Research Officer (attested 1976–1988) and holding an attested position there in 2002.

P. K. Mukhopadhyay is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He served as Professor of Philosophy at Jadavpur University and was a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 2009).

P. N. Pattabhirama Sastri (1908–1992) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under A. Chinnaswami Sastri (attested 1944). He served as an Assistant at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1941) and Reader in Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (~1952–1967).

Pramod P. Joglekar is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Editor and Member of the Regulating Council at Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (2020–2025) and as Professor of Bioarchaeology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).

P. P. Subrahmanya Sastri was an Indologist who earned an M.A. from the University of Madras and a B.A. from the University of Oxford. He served as Curator of the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library, Head of Sanskrit at Presidency University, and Professor at Presidency College.
P. Perumal is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He worked as a part-time conservator at Saraswathi Mahal Library in 1980 and earned an M.L.I.Sc from Madurai Kamaraj University in 1985.
P. Pratap Kumar (born 1952) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. In 2010, he was attested as a Professor at the University of KwaZulu-Natal and as a Visiting Professor at Colorado College.
P. S. Chandrasekharan is an Indology scholar. He pursued Ph.D. studies at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi (attested 2026).

P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri (1890–1978) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Madras. He served as Professor at Bishop Heber College, Assistant Editor of the Tamil Lexicon, Principal of Rajah's College, and Department Head at Annamalai University.

P. Swaminathan is an Indologist who completed an M.Litt. at the University of Madras by 1956 under M.A. supervisor V. Raghavan. He was a Lecturer in Sanskrit at the National Sanskrit University (attested 1965).
P. T. Narasimhachar (1905–1998) was an Indology scholar. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1923–1926), where he was taught by Mysore Hiriyanna.
P. V. Ramanujaswami was an Indologist. He served at the Sri Venkateswara Oriental Research Institute, where he held the posts of Director (attested 1944) and अध्यक्षः (attested 1954).

Padma Subrahmanyam (born 1943) is an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. She studied at Ethiraj College for Women, Stella Maris College, and Annamalai University (~1972–1979), where she conducted research supervised by T. N. Ramachandran.

Padmanabh S. Jaini (1923–2021) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under John Brough. He was a Professor and later Professor Emeritus at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 1977–2016).
Pagorn Singsuriya is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Chulalongkorn University. He held an attested position in Humanities at Mahidol University in 2021.

Palden Gyal is a scholar of Tibetology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who earned degrees from Duke, Harvard, and Columbia (Ph.D. 2018–2025). As of 2026, he is a Postdoctoral Fellow at Columbia University's Heyman Center for the Humanities.

Pallabi Bagchi is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned a B.A. at Jadavpur University and completed her Ph.D. (2021–2025) at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, where she served as a teaching assistant from 2022 to 2025.
Palmer Boyd (1840–1875) was an Indologist who studied under Edward Byles Cowell and completed a B.A. at Trinity College (1867–1871). He held a post at Trinity College, Cambridge.

Palmira Brummett (born 1950) is a historian and archaeologist educated at the University of Chicago and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. She was a professor at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (~1988–2011) and a visiting professor at Brown University (2011–2016).
